starters.title: Ideal Snow Day
starters.starter: What’s your ideal plan for a snow day if school gets canceled?
starters.stem: If I had a snow day, I would start by…, then I would…, and finally I would…
followups: Would you spend it mostly alone or with people?
Has your favorite snow-day activity changed since you were younger?

starters.title: Cold vs. Mild Days
starters.starter: Do you prefer really cold winter days or mild gray ones? Why?
followups: Which type of weather makes you more productive?
Which one is harder to deal with at school?

starters.title: Winter Habits
starters.starter: What winter tradition or habit do you enjoy, even if it’s small?
starters.stem: One winter habit I like is ___ because ___.
followups: Is it something you do alone or with others?
Do you think you’ll keep that habit as an adult?

starters.title: Seasonal Food/Drinks
starters.starter: Is there a winter food or drink you look forward to every year?
followups: Who makes it or where do you get it?
Does the taste remind you of anything?

starters.title: Annoying Winter Tasks
starters.starter: What winter chore or task do you wish you didn’t have to do?
followups: How do you make it less annoying?
Is there anyone who actually enjoys that chore?

starters.title: Redesigning Winter Break
starters.starter: If you could redesign winter break to make it better, what would you change?
starters.stem: If I redesigned winter break, I would ___ so that ___.
followups: Would you make it longer or organized differently?
How would school feel different afterward?

starters.title: Most Annoying Weather
starters.starter: What type of winter weather is the most annoying, and why?
starters.stem: The winter weather that bothers me most is ___ because ___.
followups: Does it affect your mood or your routine more?
Which weather is the easiest for you to handle?

starters.title: Childhood Winter Activities
starters.starter: What is something fun you used to do in winter as a kid that you don’t do anymore?
starters.stem: When I was younger, I used to ___, but now I don’t because ___.
followups: Would you try it again now?
What made it fun back then?

starters.title: Winter Clothing
starters.starter: What winter clothing item makes you feel the coziest or most comfortable?
starters.stem: The winter clothing I like most is ___ because ___.
followups: Do you care more about warmth or style?
Is there something you’d add to your perfect winter outfit?

starters.title: All-Day Outdoor Winter Challenge
starters.starter: If you had to spend a whole day outside in winter, what would you want to do?
starters.stem: If I had to stay outside, I’d spend my time ___, ___, and ___.
followups: What would be the hardest part?
Would you want anyone with you?

starters.title: Winter and Mood
starters.starter: Do you think winter affects people’s moods or energy levels?
starters.stem: I think winter affects people by making them feel ___ because ___.
followups: Does winter affect you personally?
Is there a way to fix or balance those feelings?

starters.title: Best Recent Winter Memory
starters.starter: What’s the best winter memory you’ve had in the last few years?
starters.stem: A favorite winter memory I have is ___ because ___.
followups: Who was with you?
Would you want that to happen again?

starters.title: Winter Activity You Wish You Liked
starters.starter: What winter activity do you wish you liked, but you really don’t?
starters.stem: I wish I liked ___, but I don’t because ___.
followups: What would make it more enjoyable?
Do your friends like it?

starters.title: Winter Destination
starters.starter: If you could teleport to any winter location for a day, where would you go?
followups: What would you want to see or do there?
Would you go alone or with someone?

starters.title: Relaxing Winter Moments
starters.starter: What winter sound, sight, or moment feels relaxing to you?
starters.stem: A winter moment that relaxes me is ___ because ___.
followups: When was the last time you noticed it?
Does it help you focus, calm down, or something else?

starters.title: Thankful Round
starters.text: Share what you are thankful for this year. Take turns adding more than one thing so the talk keeps going.
followUps: What changed from last year?
Who helped you the most?
How did you show thanks?

starters.title: Leftovers Plan
starters.text: Plan how to use Thanksgiving leftovers. Compare ideas like sandwiches, soups, or sharing with neighbors.
followUps: Which idea is fastest to make?
What ingredients do you need?
Who will enjoy each idea the most?

starters.title: Parade or Football?
starters.text: Decide what to watch first: the parade or the football game. Explain reasons and make a schedule.
followUps: What time does each start?
Who wants to watch each one?
Can you split the time fairly?

starters.title: Travel Tales
starters.text: Talk about a past Thanksgiving travel story. Describe what went smoothly and what was tricky.
followUps: What would you change next time?
Who helped solve the problem?
What was the best part of the trip?

starters.title: Favorite Tradition
starters.text: Describe a family tradition and why it matters. Invite the other person to share theirs and compare.
followUps: How did the tradition start?
What makes it special?
Would you change or add anything?

starters.title: Helping Out
starters.text: Plan how to help before or after the meal. Divide tasks like setting the table, dishes, or packing leftovers.
followUps: Which tasks match each person’s strengths?
What needs to happen first?
How will you know the job is done well?

starters.title: Recipe Swap
starters.text: Talk about a favorite Thanksgiving recipe. Explain steps and ask for tips to make it better.
followUps: Which step is most important?
How do you know it is done?
What can go wrong and how do you fix it?

starters.title: Gratitude Cards
starters.text: Plan to make gratitude cards for guests or community helpers. Decide what to write and how to deliver them.
followUps: Who should get a card and why?
What message will you include?
How will you deliver them?

starters.title: Welcoming a New Guest
starters.text: A friend is joining Thanksgiving for the first time. Plan how to make them feel included.
followUps: What info should you share ahead of time?
What activities can include everyone?
How will you check in during the meal?

starters.title: Small Conflict, Quick Repair
starters.text: Two people want the last slice of pie. Talk through a fair solution without arguing.
followUps: What options are fair?
How can both people feel heard?
What words can you use to stay calm?
